sentences.text:
The appellant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.35/2022 for the offences punishable under sections 376, 294, 506, 342, 376(2)(chh) of IPC and Sections 3(1)(d), 3(1)(dha),
3(2)(V), 3(1)(w)(ii), 3(1)(w- i) of the SC/ST Act registered at Police Station Chachoda, District Guna.
The appellant is in judicial custody since 08.12.2022.
The charge against him is of having raped the prosecutrix who is a member of the depressed classes of society.
Undisputed facts in this case are that on 16.09.2022 the incident is stated to have taken place.
On 10.10.2022, a complaint was given written by hand by the complainant herself on the basis of which the F.I.R. was registered.
Only the co-accused name is mentioned in the written complaint and the F.I.R. as the person who had raped the prosecutrix.

On 10.10.2022 itself, 161 statement of the prosecutrix was recorded in which again,
she has not named the appellant herein.

Four days later on 14.10.2022 a supplementary statement of the prosecutrix under 161 Cr.P.C. was recorded in which she, for the first time, takes the name of the appellant also as the co-accused in the rape case.
The same thing is reiterated by the prosecutrix before the Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 17.10.2022.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has falsely been implicated as an afterthought almost more than a month after the alleged incident.

He further submits that the F.I.R.
is delayed by more than 20 days and no plausible reason is given for the delay.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State submits that the prosecutrix has clearly stated against the appellant in the 164 statement before the JMFC.

Be that as it may, firstly, no reason for the delay in registration of F.I.R.
by almost 20 days is given in the F.I.R.
Secondly, the written complaint dated 10.10.2022 of the prosecutrix does not mention the name of the appellant and neither does it attribute any role to him.

Neither is his name mentioned in the 161 statement recorded on 10.10.2022, thereafter, almost a month later, the supplementary statement is recorded in which she attributed the role to the appellant herein in the said offence and likewise, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
Normally, this Court would have relied upon the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. if the name of the appellant was not mentioned in the F.I.R.

However, in this case, the distinction lies with the fact that the prosecutrix herself gave a written complaint on 10.10.2022 in which the appellant's name is not mentioned and the said written complaint is reduced into an F.I.R.
The reliance on her 164 statement in opposition to the contents of F.I.R. is where the F.I.R. is recorded on an oral statement or an oral narration by the complainant to the police.

Under the circumstances, in view of what has been argued and considered hereinabove, the appeal is allowed and it is directed that the appellant herein shall be enlarged on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum o f Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.
Certified copy as per rules.
